title.instructions: Use a concise three-to-five-word Title Case noun phrase describing the task. Do not use a leading verb, branch prefix, quotes, or markdown.

branchName.instructions: Use `<type>/<kebab-case-description>`. Choose the narrowest fitting type from `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `style`, or `revert`. Keep the description concise and use valid Git ref characters.

commitMessage.instructions: Return only one Conventional Commit message for the staged diff. Use `<type>(<scope>): <imperative summary>` and keep the first line at 72 characters or fewer. Choose from `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `style`, or `revert`. Use a scope such as `game`, `audio`, `player`, `floors`, `title`, `ui`, `e2e`, `build`, or `assets` when it adds useful context; otherwise omit it. For a breaking change, add `!` before the colon and include a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Use `feat` for a new user-visible capability, `fix` or `perf` for patch-level behavior, and a breaking marker for a major change. Describe only the staged change. Describe source behavior without narrating generated `dist/` filenames. Do not add surrounding prose or generated-by footers.

pullRequest.instructions: Return a concise pull request title followed by a GitHub-flavored Markdown body. Cover the complete branch. Use `## Summary` for the behavior and implementation, then `## Testing` with a checklist of checks that were run. Call out breaking changes explicitly. Describe source behavior without narrating generated `dist/` filenames. Do not add surrounding prose or generated-by footers.
